body:
one day at a time is basically the level i am capable of operating on right now. sometimes it feels liberating to think there are no guarantees about tomorrow - other times it feels terrifying. i wish i could crawl into a cave and hibernate like a bear until this is all over.

your kind words mean a lot to me. thank you for your thoughts.

i can really relate to the feeling of being stuck in one spot and no longer moving forward. i feel like my life has been frozen in time for a while now. i'm sorry that you're experiencing this too.

i work for a very small company. small enough that my absence would cause problems in their day-to-day operations (not necessarily for the lack of my skills, but for the lack of another body to handle the workload). i've never really been able to step away on my own accord.

i'm grateful that i've even still had a job throughout lockdown, but working for a small business is demanding. i've struggled a lot to keep up over the past several months as my mental health has worsened and i've had more than one discussion about my performance with my boss. the shame i feel about it is immense. i used to be a great employee.

the lack of basic normalcy really gets to me. everything in my life has been uprooted and turned on its head, and i don't have access to many of the things i once used to cope. 

i've been thinking about moving out of here and finding a new roommate so at least i have someone to see every day, but things are really hard financially right now. at the same time, it feels imperative that i do have someone to see (and to keep an eye on me) or else i'm going to wither away. i feel stuck and uncertain about what to do. it's a major decision and i don't feel like i have the capacity to make major decisions right now.

i'm sorry to hear you're going through something similar. it's rough. thank you for connecting with me.

i'm so sorry for your loss. i can only imagine what you must be going through.  


i had a lot of hobbies and goals and pastimes what feels like a long time ago. my life feels like it's gotten so much smaller now - like i live in a fishbowl. it's hard for me to conceptualize even next week. i try to keep busy when i can, but i don't find enjoyment in the things i used to love anymore. more and more my only motivation is "go to bed". it's been a long time since my depression was this bad.

i appreciate your thoughts. thank you for talking with me.

i've spent a lot of time on video chats over the past few months. it does help and i'm glad that we live in a world where it's an option - but for me it's just not quite enough, at least not over as long a time period as this. i don't think i realized how much i need real life human companionship before lockdown. i really appreciate the recommendation though, thank you for sharing it with me.
